ideas.title: Leave it up to the AI
ideas.detail: A post-it you can put on a frame (toggle in the screen details): the builder generates a standard, conventional page for it from the title, purpose, ideas and yarn. No drawing needed; the review stops asking for one; the export says so. Example: the Guide.

ideas.title: Tell the agent, in every view
ideas.detail: One button per view (board, screen editor, connection editor, plan, ideas panel, outline, review, test flow) copies a prompt naming exactly what you are looking at, with the brief the running app serves for it (/api/projects/:id/brief), the skills (/api/skills) and the rules (/api/checklist.md). The agent reads the live board and writes back through the local API.

ideas.title: Landing page: your boards and a way to start one
ideas.detail: The app opens on a landing page in the design of the site: the name and tagline, Start a board (a name and New blank board, or New board with your agent), and Your boards with screen counts and the last opened one marked. The brand at the top left brings you back. Built 2026-09-26.

ideas.title: Interactive tutorial (to do, later)
ideas.detail: Five or six panels that teach the app, opened from the landing page: the board, pins and yarn, the plan, Review flow, Test flow, and Tell the agent. Not built yet; the user asked to keep it as a to-do.

ideas.title: Three build levels for a new board
ideas.detail: A three-position switch in the handoff dialog (New board with your agent, and Plan it with your agent on an empty board): Just the list (ideas in the pool, a to-do list of what to draw and connect; no frames, no strings), Frames and strings (planned frames with the yarn already tied through provisional pins; the default, so later changes are tweaks), Built out (frames and strings with every frame left to the AI; take the post-it off the one or two pages you draw yourself). Choosing a level rewrites and re-copies the prompt.

ideas.title: The prompt is three lines
ideas.detail: Subject, the address of the brief the app serves for exactly this task, and “Anything I add below this line is part of the task.” The brief is the instruction file: task, skills, rules and the slice of the board. Only the address changes between views.

ideas.title: Strings before drawings
ideas.detail: A planned frame can carry provisional pins (placeholder spots down its right side) with real yarn, written by the agent or added in the editor (Add a pin, Place on an idea). When a drawing lands, the editor shows Place on the drawing for each waiting pin; click it, click the drawing, the yarn follows. Review flow warns (pin-not-placed) until every waiting pin is placed.

ideas.title: Planned cards keep a fixed box
ideas.detail: A planned frame is a 2:1 box in board units, the same the layout math assumes. Zoomed out under 40% it shows only its tape and code; tape titles trim to the tape. Thirty planned frames fit the window as a readable map.

ideas.title: Place a pin before the drawing
ideas.detail: On a frame without a drawing, Add a pin and Place (on an idea) create a provisional pin at a slot instead of asking for a click on the drawing. The stage says how many pins wait with their yarn.

ideas.title: Place on the drawing strip
ideas.detail: When a frame that has provisional pins gets its drawing, a strip above the caption lists them; click one, then click where it goes. Dragging a provisional pin places it too.

ideas.title: Pin not placed yet
ideas.detail: A warning for a provisional pin on a frame that now has a drawing: open the frame and click where the pin goes; its yarn follows.

ideas.title: One place to bring sketches in
ideas.detail: The library leads with the drop box: drop sketches, click to browse files, Add a folder (every image in it, once), or Connect a folder to watch it. No separate folder card.

ideas.title: A crowded board rests quietly
ideas.detail: Above eight threads the yarn draws back and every label waits as a small mark. Clicking a frame brings its own threads and labels forward, fades the rest, and steps the frames it is tied to a little further apart. The step is only on screen. Clicking the cork lets go; the tape, the arrow and a double-click open a frame.

ideas.title: Left to the AI is built out
ideas.detail: A frame wearing the post-it with no drawing gets a real page: top bar, heading and lede, a main action, cards from the ideas, fields for a sign-in, a dialog for a modal, a quiet ending for a terminal screen. Test flow walks it as a site; only the redirects work. flow.md carries the same page.

ideas.title: The one-way review waits for the drawing
ideas.detail: A frame with no drawing is backlog, so its ways back are not settled. A frame left to the AI is still checked, because its page is the specification.
